clue.text: Throw out and dismiss counsel's opening in vindication — situation's about right

indicators.note: to dismiss something is to send it away, so a letter is taken out of the word for vindication

parts.note: a defence is a justification or vindication of one's conduct

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here the first letter of counsel's
about means going around, so the word for situation goes around the letter for right

parts.note: a state is a situation or condition

explanation.surface: A lawyer's vindication of a client is swept aside: their opening argument rejected and the case turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismiss' removes C (the first letter of counsel's, signalled by 'opening') from DEFENCE, leaving DEFENE; 'about' puts STATE round R to make STRATE. 'Throw out' looks like a summary of the legal story but is literally out of a window.
explanation.definitionFit: Defenestration is ejection through a window, and by extension any brusque expulsion from office.

clue.text: Fresh garment's in a state

parts.note: fresh means new
a jersey is a knitted garment for the upper body

explanation.surface: A new knitted top is all the rage in some state or other.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey is one of the fifty states of the USA, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Difficulty supporting mum's plant

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece is written beneath, so the word for difficulty comes after the word for mum

parts.note: mum as in keeping mum means silence, and SH is the call for silence
a rub is a difficulty or snag, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: Some problem is propping up the plant that belongs to mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' reads as mother but means silent, giving SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody plant smaller than a tree, with several stems.

clue.text: Briefly explain two cricketing terms

parts.note: in cricket a run is a single scored point
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a short explanation of a pair of baffling cricket words.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is the British bat-and-ball game: a RUN is a point scored by running between the wickets and an OVER is a set of six deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: To run over something is to go through it quickly, recapping or summarising it.

clue.text: Source of oil right amidst bike races, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the letters are said aloud and the answer is the sound they make

parts.note: R for right is put amidst TT, the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorbike races

explanation.surface: An oil source turns up, rumour has it, in the middle of motorcycle racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amidst' puts R inside TT; spoken, those letters run together to make the answer's sound. The TT is the motorbike race series held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian tea tree yields an antiseptic essential oil used in cosmetics and remedies.

clue.text: Source of clipping containing some minor points?

definitions.text: Source of clipping containing some minor points?

parts.words: Source of clipping containing some minor points?
parts.note: the whole clue describes a small cutting tool for the fingers, whose blades end in tiny tips, as though it were a document with minor points

explanation.surface: A newspaper clipping that covers some trivial matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipping' suggests a press cutting and 'points' arguments, but both are literal: the tool clips and has small sharp points.
explanation.definitionFit: Small curved scissors are used for trimming fingernails, and their blades have fine points.

clue.text: Aviators' song was triumphant

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
crew is an old past tense of crow, and to crow is to exult in triumph

explanation.surface: Pilots sing a victorious song.
explanation.definitionFit: The aircrew are the people who fly and staff an aeroplane, so aviators' answers to aircrew used attributively.

clue.text: Fugitives avoiding a feature of airports

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of, so the letter given by the clue's a is left out

parts.note: runaways are people who have fled, fugitives

explanation.surface: Escapees steer clear of an airport feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names the kind of feature; the answer is the plural of it, as airports usually have several.
explanation.definitionFit: Runways are the paved strips on which aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: Theatre worker: coach one in crib?

parts.note: a stage, short for stagecoach, is a horse-drawn coach

indicators.note: in says the letter for one is placed inside the word for crib

parts.note: a manger is a feeding trough or crib
A means one, as in a pound

explanation.surface: A drama worker wonders whether to train someone in a cheat sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a verb (train) but is a stagecoach; 'crib' looks like copying but is a manger.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage manager runs the backstage side of a theatre production.

clue.text: Material issuing from forbidding era (though not book

indicators.note: not says the letter for book is left out of the phrase

parts.note: a bleak age is a grim, forbidding era

explanation.surface: Something seeps out from a grim period, but no volume.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is BLEAK AGE; the parenthesis is just punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Leakage is the stuff that escapes from a container through a hole or crack.

clue.text: 50% of each of Bach variations encountered in part of Germany

indicators.note: fifty per cent of each word means the first half of Bach and the first half of variations

explanation.surface: Half of every Bach set of variations turns up in a German region.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of BACH is BA and half of VARIATIONS is VARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Bavaria is the large southern state of Germany, with Munich as its capital.

clue.text: Style of clothing that is sufficient for attractive girl

parts.note: the cut of a garment is its style
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A fashion that is good enough for a pretty young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is informal for a sweet, good-looking person, especially a young woman.

clue.text: Take the place of Society peers, due to be dumped

indicators.note: dumped suggests things thrown down in a heap, so these letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: Lords who are about to be thrown out are replaced by society figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be dumped' shuffles PEERS and DUE into UPERSEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede is to replace or displace something older.

clue.text: Type of payment? Distributed a receipt before end of sale

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters of a and receipt are scattered into a new order
the end of a word is its last letter, here that of sale

explanation.surface: A receipt is handed out before the close of a sale; what sort of payment was it?
explanation.definitionFit: Piece rate is a pay system in which workers are paid per item produced rather than by the hour.

clue.text: Result of over-indulgence in emergency supply?

definitions.meaning: a roll of fat round the waist from eating too much
the extra wheel carried in a car in case of a puncture

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the spare wheel kept for punctures and, jokingly, a bulge of belly fat round the middle.

clue.text: I have to follow a vehicle, describing poor handling

indicators.note: to follow means to come after, so I've is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone complains about having to trail behind a vehicle that is being driven badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive treatment is cruel or harmful mistreatment, the opposite of careful care.

clue.text: Dead upset about English navy on a permanent basis

indicators.note: about means around, so the turned word goes round the other letters
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word for dead is read from bottom to top

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king
RN is the Royal Navy, the British navy

explanation.surface: A dead man, distraught over the English navy, stays that way forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LATE into ETAL, and 'about' puts it round E and RN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting forever, without end.

clue.text: Some call a maverick a domesticated animal

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people would call a nonconformist a tamed beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American camelid domesticated for wool and as a pack animal.

clue.text: Writer, upset, interrupting fat cat

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the turned writer sits inside the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the writer's name is read backwards

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: An agitated author bursts in on a fat cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns POE into EOP; 'fat cat' looks like one phrase but splits into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The leopard is a large spotted big cat of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Bitterness shown by one daughter in Manchester, say

indicators.note: in says the letters for one and daughter go inside the phrase

parts.note: Manchester is an example of a city, so it is a city
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An only daughter living in Manchester shows resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks Manchester as an example: A CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidity is sourness or sharpness, of taste or of temper.

clue.text: Mostly work fast, getting rich

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word for work is dropped

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially of music
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone works mainly at speed and grows wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but is a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means lavishly wealthy or luxurious.

clue.text: Meeting's to test the patience of saint

parts.note: to try someone is to tax their patience

explanation.surface: A rendezvous would strain even a saint's patience.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret meeting between lovers.

clue.text: Beethoven symphony — about time for stimulating stuff!

indicators.note: about means around, so the symphony's name goes round the letter for time

parts.note: Eroica is the name of Beethoven's Third Symphony

explanation.surface: A Beethoven symphony is said to be just the thing for excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is literature or art meant to arouse sexually.

clue.text: Having some points about half of pine wood

indicators.note: about means around, so the prickly word goes round the half word

parts.note: spiny means bearing spines or sharp points

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is two letters, here the back half of pine

explanation.surface: A pine-wood tree with sharp tips is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes NE, the last two letters of pine, which SPINY goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinney is a small wood or copse.

clue.text: Girl taking pudding showing greed

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
rice pudding, often just called rice

explanation.surface: A girl helping herself to dessert shows she is a glutton.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is extreme greed for wealth.

clue.text: Important time for the old Russian postal service?

definitions.text: Important time for the old Russian postal service?

parts.words: Important time for the old Russian postal service?
parts.note: a memorable occasion, read as a day for mail from the Soviet Reds, communists

explanation.surface: Asks what a big day would be for the Soviet post office.
explanation.walkthrough: Red was the label for Soviet communists, so the post of the old USSR would deal in Red letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a special or memorable day, from saints' days printed in red in calendars.
